claims.evidence: Three triple-SILAC experiments (IAV_SUMO1, IAV_SUMO2, HS_SUMO2 = archive prefixes). Per experiment the three labelled cultures (20 dishes each) were lysed, mixed 1:1:1; ~1% was analysed as the crude sample and ~99% TAP-purified (PRIDE protocol; Document S1 "TAP Procedure"). Crude and purified are physically distinct measured samples (batch rule 16), so each (culture x crude/purified) has its own source name; one name per physical sample, never reused.

claims.value: 13 gel slices per sample; fraction = slice order of the .raw member names (_01.._13, pur01..pur13, cru21..cru33)
claims.evidence: PRIDE protocol: "the gel was sliced into 13 sections". Each archive has exactly 13 .raw members. MaxQuant summary.txt lists all 26 raw files per search, assigned to experiments CRU (13 *cru*) and PUR (13 *pur*). comment[data file] names the .raw member inside its zip archive (the archive itself is the deposited file).
Each gel slice of each sample was injected once: 13 .raw members per archive, one per slice, and each raw file appears once in summary.txt; no repeated injections deposited.

limitations: comment[precursor mass tolerance] = not available: MaxQuant 1.3.0.5 parameters.txt / summary.txt and Document S1 parameter table do not record the first/main-search precursor tolerance and no mqpar.xml was deposited. Consequence: parse_sdrf convert-openms cannot read a precursor tolerance (campaign precedents PXD014368, PXD002388).

comment[reduction reagent] / comment[alkylation reagent] = not available: in-gel digestion is cited "essentially as described previously (Shevchenko et al., 2006)" without reagents; the fixed Carbamidomethyl (C) search implies an alkylation but no reagent is named.

The data files are .raw members inside six deposited zip archives; comment[data file] names the member (e.g. 20130807_MTFG_IAVS1pur_01.raw inside IAV_SUMO1_pur_Archive.zip). The archives are >4 GiB without zip64 records (32-bit offsets wrap); members were listed from the central directory, not extracted.

Document S1 states two MaxQuant analyses per IAV experiment ("global" and "slice-by-slice"); only one txt output per experiment was deposited (CRU/PUR experiment design = global). Both used the parameter table shown, so the modification and tolerance columns hold for either.

PRIDE data processing protocol says UniProtKB human + IAV reference proteomes; the deposited search output shows the viral entries as GenBank accessions (gi|...|AAA43352.1 matrix protein, ACF54602.1 nucleocapsid protein, ...) from HUMAN_WSN.fasta. Recorded; no SDRF column depends on it.

Observation, HS_SUMO2: trace influenza NP (17 peptides) and NS1 (4 peptides) are quantified in the heat-shock search with the IAV-like channel pattern (crude log2 M/L -2.56, H/M +2.55 for NP), but at ~0.1 per mille of channel intensity in crude versus ~47 per mille in the IAV experiments (~400-fold lower; viral_abundance.txt). M1, HA, PB2 are absent. This is consistent with low-level contamination or LC carryover of previously run IAV SILAC peptides, not infection; the protocol states no infection in the heat-shock experiment, so HS rows are annotated "uninfected". The channel map (L TAP only, M TAP-SUMO2 37°C, H TAP-SUMO2 43°C) is supported by the protocol, the Fig. S5 axis label and the SUMO-bait enrichment pattern.

MOI 2 PFU/cell, 10 h infection (IAV) and 43°C for 30 min (heat shock) are recorded here and in the report, not in SDRF columns (no fitting licensed column). Passage number and sample storage temperature are not stated (not available).
Review: per the caller, the independent sdrf-adversarial-review is run externally (REVIEW_PENDING_EXTERNAL); no self-review or review-gate approval was performed.
